but many are deaf to my voice, and hardened. More people listen more willingly to the world than to God: they more easily follow the appetite of their own flesh than the good pleasure of God. The world promises temporal and small things, and is served with great greed: I promise the highest and eternal things, and the hearts of mortals grow sluggish. Who serves and obeys me in all things with such great care, as the world and its masters are served? <margin>Isaiah 23</margin> "Be ashamed, O Sidon," says the sea <note>Sidon was a great merchant city; the sea here laments the loss of its strength or the vanity of earthly commerce</note>. And if you ask the cause, hear why. For a small stipend <note>original: "praebenda", a source of income or a church office</note>, a long journey is run: for eternal life, many hardly lift a foot once from the earth. A cheap price is sought: for a single coin, men sometimes disgracefully quarrel: for a vain thing and a small promise, they do not fear to be fatigued day and night.

4. But, oh shame! for the unchangeable good, for the inestimable reward, for the highest honor and unending glory, they are too lazy to be fatigued even in the slightest. Be ashamed therefore, sluggish and complaining servant, that those people are found more ready for destruction than you are for life. They rejoice more in vanity than you do in truth. Indeed, they are sometimes frustrated in their hope: but my promise fails no one, nor does it send away empty the one who trusts in me. What I have promised, I will give; what I have said, I will fulfill; provided that a person remains faithful in my love until the end. I am the rewarder of all good men, and the strong tester of all devout souls.

5. Write my words in your heart, and consider them diligently: for they will be very necessary in the time of temptation. What you do not understand when you read, you shall know in the day of visitation <note>the time when God's presence is felt, either in grace or judgment</note>. I am accustomed to visit my elect in two ways: namely, by temptation and by consolation. And I read two lessons to them daily: one, by rebuking their vices; the other, by exhorting them to the increase of virtues. He who has my words and despises them, has one who shall judge him on the last day.

<summary>Christ rebukes the soul for serving the world and its fleeting rewards with more zeal than it serves God. He promises that His eternal rewards never fail those who endure temptation and remain faithful.</summary>
<keywords>divine promise, vanity of the world, spiritual sloth, Sidon, eternal life, temptation, consolation, judgment</keywords>
